title: Committee of Supply – Head X (Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head X (Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth)

sections.label: SG50 celebration initiatives and fund
sections.summary: Over 500 initiatives marked Singapore's 50th year of Independence, and the SG50 celebration fund disbursed about $10 million to ground-up project organisers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: More than 500 initiatives were organised to celebrate Singapore's 50th year of Independence, including the biggest National Day Parade and the Future of Us exhibition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The SG50 celebration fund disbursed about $10 million to organisers of these ground-up projects.

sections.label: Our Singapore Fund
sections.summary: Our Singapore Fund will support projects building caring, resilience, can-do spirit and unity, with a fund size of up to $25 million set up by the second half of this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our Singapore Fund will support projects that build the spirit of caring and resilience, nurture our can-do spirit and promote unity and our sense of being Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The total fund size will be up to $25 million and will be set up by the second half of this year.

sections.label: MENDAKI Future Ready Unit
sections.summary: In October last year, MENDAKI set up the Future Ready Unit to help the Malay/Muslim community prepare for the future economy via SkillsFuture opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In October last year, MENDAKI set up the Future Ready Unit to help the Malay/Muslim community to better prepare for the future economy by optimising opportunities arising from the SkillsFuture initiative.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim educational standing survey
sections.summary: The General Household Survey 2015 report suggests the Singapore Malay/Muslim community is in a better educational standing than five years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our Singapore Malay/Muslim community is in a better educational standing compared to five years ago, as suggested by the General Household Survey 2015 report.

sections.label: MENDAKI plans and MBMF
sections.summary: The question asks what MENDAKI's plans are to further strengthen its educational programmes and outreach, especially with the increased Mosque Building and MENDAKI Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What are MENDAKI's plans to further strengthen its educational programmes and outreach, especially with the increased Mosque Building and MENDAKI Fund (MBMF)?

sections.label: MBMF contribution increase
sections.summary: An announcement was made about increased MBMF contributions, which support mosque development, religious programmes and educational and social programmes by Malay/Muslim bodies like MENDAKI Foundation and AMP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Recently, an announcement was made about the increase in the MBMF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The fund supports the development and enhancements to mosques, religious programmes as well as various educational and social programmes by Malay/Muslim bodies like the MENDAKI Foundation and the Association of Muslim Professionals (AMP).

sections.label: MUIS MENDAKI family support, zakat
sections.summary: Asks how MUIS and MENDAKI will assist families, address root causes, and what share of annual zakat goes to such families.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: How else will Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura (MUIS) and MENDAKI assist and also sort out the root causes faced by these families and also provide more support for them in a targeted way?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Also, can I find out what proportion of our annual zakat collection is being disbursed to such families?

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   In his reply to my query in this Chamber on whether the Malay/Muslim Community Development Fund (MMCDF) can be extended to the mosques, the Minister said that this cannot be done as mosques are not considered to be Malay/Muslim bodies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, he added that mosques can receive this fund if their social programmes are run in cooperation with Government bodies or other Malay/Muslim organisations.

sections.label: Extending MMCDF to mosques
sections.summary: Asks the Minister to consider extending the Malay/Muslim Community Development Fund to mosques and to clarify Malay/Muslim organisation criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the name of this spirit of partnership, I would to like to ask that the Minister and the Government consider the proposal that this fund be extended to the mosques, so that this MMCDF can bring further benefits towards the development of the Malay/Muslim community in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, can the Minister clarify what are the criteria that are being used to categorise an institution or organisation as a Malay/Muslim organisation (MMO)?

sections.label: Update on community numbers
sections.summary: Asks for an update on current community numbers and whether targeted interventions have positively impacted these families.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: Can we have an update on the current numbers that we face in the community and to assess if targeted interventions that have been implemented along the way have been positive and have impacted these families?

sections.label: Cinta Abadi framework update
sections.summary: Asks for an update on the Cinta Abadi enrichment framework for Malay/Muslim couples in their first 10 years of marriage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: At last year's Committee of Supply (COS) debate, the Minister-in-Charge of Muslim Affairs mentioned that the Ministry of Social and Family Development will be developing a Cinta Abadi enrichment framework targeted at Malay/Muslim couples in their first 10 years of marriage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can the Minister give an update on this development?

sections.label: Update on Muslim Affairs measures
sections.summary: Asks the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs for an update on some of these measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs give an update on some of these measures?

sections.label: Reviewing Syariah Court, AMLA, MMDR
sections.summary: Asks whether there are plans to review Syariah Court processes and amend AMLA or MMDR to clarify and streamline legal procedures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The last amendment of AMLA came into effect in 2009.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is important to review whether the provisions match the existing circumstances of the community, as well as the current practice of the Court.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Issues, such as jurisdiction, the hakam process, the talak declaration process, may be some of the areas that the Court may wish to review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is useful to look at the existing procedures and forms and amend AMLA and MMDR accordingly, to make the process more expedient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In light of the above, could the Minister share if there are plans to review and enhance the Syariah Court processes and amend AMLA or MMDR to clarify and streamline the legal procedures?

sections.label: Mosque Development Programme progress
sections.summary: MP asks the Minister to elaborate on the Mosque Development Programme, the Maarof and Yusof Ishak mosques, and Tampines North and Al-Istighfar plans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Minister announced an increase in the MBMF contributions last month and shared plans to improve the mosque institutions in the coming years, by increasing prayer space and improving the infrastructure for the convenience of the congregants, especially the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister elaborate on the progress of the Mosque Development Programme?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In addition, can the Minister give an update on construction of the Maarof Mosque in Jurong West and the Yusof Ishak Mosque in Woodlands?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: During last year's COS, the Minister announced that we will build the Tampines North mosque and are looking at ways to deal with the shortage of prayer space in the Al-Istighfar mosque in Pasir Ris.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide more details about these plans and share with us what the community can expect in the next few years?

sections.label: FY2016 PA budget size
sections.summary: The FY2016 budget is nearly $900 million, a 34% increase from FY2014, though FY2015 was larger due to SG50 and residents' facilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While we understand that the financial year (FY) 2015 Budget was much larger than usual due to the SG50 activities and building residents' facilities, the FY 2016 budget is still very high, at nearly $900 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is a significant 34% increase from FY2014.

sections.label: PA and opposition engagement channels
sections.summary: An MP says PA quarters advance the Ruling Party, and that MND and HDB recognise only PA bodies like CCCs and RCs as proper channels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An unhealthy culture seems to have developed within some quarters of PA who sees its role to include advancing the Ruling Party politically and undermining the work of Opposition Members of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As Opposition Members, when we try to advance our residents' welfare through infrastructure projects, we learn that Government agencies like the Ministry of National Development (MND) and the Housing and Development Board will only recognise PA organisations, such as Citizens Consultative Committees (CCCs) and Residents' Committees (RCs) as "the proper channels".

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When I tried to simply get information from MND on the plans for private estate upgrading projects within Aljunied Group Representation Constituency (GRC), the Ministry referred me to the CCC.

sections.label: Online disinformation and youth radicalisation
sections.summary: An MP asks the Ministry to explain online chatter, measures to engage young people, and plans to build national resilience against youth radicalisation from online disinformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The online chatter is disconcerting, to say the least, and leads us to wonder how digital communications may have poisoned the chalice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I hope the Ministry would be able to shed some light on this recent phenomenon and advise the House on the measures being taken to engage young people so that we understand their concerns and lead them on to become better Singaporeans who care for their own and the community at large.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Only by doing so would we be able to chart our way forward to SG100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And moving on to the growing threat of radicalisation amongst the young due to the pervasiveness of online disinformation, what are the Ministry's plans to continue to build up national resilience and cohesiveness to safeguard unity in Singapore?

sections.label: Arts access for vulnerable groups
sections.summary: An MP asks how the Ministry enables the disabled, less well-off and vulnerable young to engage in the arts, and about funding and digital platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share how it has made it possible for the disabled, the less well-off and the vulnerable young to be engaged in the arts scene and how the Ministry plans to expand this so that they can contribute to and fully experience the arts and cultural life?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I further urge the Ministry to extend more funding to worthy ground-up initiatives to engage the less fortunate in arts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: On the subject of potential digital platforms, has the Ministry also looked at the potential for it to transform and expand the arts scene and in reaching out to more Singaporeans?

sections.label: NAC traditional arts plan
sections.summary: An MP asks for an update on NAC's traditional arts plan and future plans, noting $25 million in funding announced in 2015 over five years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Can the Minister give an update on how the National Arts Council's (NAC's) traditional arts plan has helped to nurture and deepen traditional arts practice in Singapore and what are the plans ahead?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: In 2015, the Government announced that it would put some $25 million in funding for traditional arts over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: These funds are used to foster audiences both at home and abroad and to improve research and documentation of traditional Asian art forms.

sections.label: Independent history grants commission
sections.summary: An independent commission of historians and heritage specialists should oversee grants to encourage critical thinking through different interpretations of history.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An independent commission made up of professional historians and heritage specialists from different institutions should be set up to oversee the grants, with the mission to encourage critical thinking through different interpretations of history.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An independent commission would signal to the public that the Government is not here to control and censure history.

sections.label: Strengthening heritage impact assessments
sections.summary: The existing legal framework over heritage impact assessments and archaeological artefacts should be strengthened, noting the URA Planning Act mandates HIAs for land development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Strengthen the existing legal framework over heritage impact assessments, or HIAs, and over artefacts from archaeological excavations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) Planning Act does make it mandatory for persons seeking to develop land to carry out HIAs.

sections.label: Artefact ownership and HIA committee
sections.summary: The law is unclear on who owns excavated artefacts, and an inter-Ministerial working committee should develop HIA requirements in consultation with civil society groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Another crucial gap in the legal framework is the issue of ownership of artefacts that are discovered in the course of archaeological excavations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The law is currently unclear on who owns the artefacts, the landowner or the state, with different implications for their protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to establish an inter-Ministerial working committee to develop HIA requirements and review the current state of heritage protection, in consultation with civil society groups like the Singapore Heritage Society, Nature Society and the International Council on Monuments and Sites (ICOMOS) Singapore.

sections.label: 2011 Arts and Culture Strategic Review
sections.summary: In 2011, the Arts and Culture Strategic Review report was unveiled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in 2011, the Arts and Culture Strategic Review (ACSR) report was unveiled.

sections.label: Government $270 million arts commitment
sections.summary: The Government committed $270 million worth of programmes under three master plans, rolled out over five years from 2012 to 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In response to the report, the Government has committed $270 million worth of programmes under three master plans, rolled out over five years from 2012 to 2016.

sections.label: Community engagement master plan programmes
sections.summary: The community engagement master plan rolled out since 2012 has seen many arts programmes organised by PA, NAC, NHB and NLB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The community engagement master plan that was rolled out since 2012 has seen a proliferation of arts programmes organised by PA, NAC, NHB and the National Library Board (NLB).

sections.label: Need for more arts intermediaries
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to develop more intermediaries to facilitate collaborations among artists, agencies and the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As such, to encourage more participation and engagement from the community, more intermediaries must be made available to facilitate fruitful collaborations among artists, related agencies and the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I, therefore, urge the Ministry to look into developing these specialists.

sections.label: Benefits of proper planning and execution
sections.summary: Proper planning and execution would foster community bonding and identity, build capacity, empower the community, and address artists' lack of physical space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If planned and executed properly, it will not only foster community bonding and identity, build capacity in a community, it also empowers the community to action and change, it will also solve one of the problems that artists and arts groups face in Singapore: the lack of physical space to work.

sections.label: Kuo Pao Kun and The Substation
sections.summary: The Substation, founded by Kuo Pao Kun, supported young artists with infrastructure and resources and encouraged creative risk-taking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One is reminded of what the late Kuo Pao Kun had said before: "Better to have a worthy failure than a mediocre success." The Substation, founded by Mr Kuo, was such an arts centre: it provided infrastructure support and resources for young artists to kickstart projects and, at the same time, provided an environment to encourage artists to take creative risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many young artists have begun their careers there, including filmmakers Royston Tan and Boo Jun Feng, and theatre director Goh Boon Teck.

sections.label: Different model for developmental arts centres
sections.summary: The speaker urges MCCY and NAC to develop a different model for developmental centres like ITI to encourage experimentation, creative processes and learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, the Intercultural Theatre Institute (ITI), are funded under the three-year Major Grant Scheme, just like other arts organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The key performance indicators of these kinds of developmental centres are different from a typical arts organisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would urge MCCY and NAC to develop a different model for these institutions that will encourage experimentation, creative processes and learning.

sections.label: Bukit Panjang Community Arts and Culture Club
sections.summary: Since the Community Arts and Culture Club formed in Bukit Panjang in 2014, many arts and culture activities have benefited over 7,000 residents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Since the formation of the Community Arts and Culture Club (CACC) in Bukit Panjang in 2014, we have organised many arts and culture activities to benefit more than 7,000 residents.

sections.label: Bukit Panjang Arts Street
sections.summary: Bukit Panjang constituency has started work to build a "Bukit Panjang Arts Street" at Bangkit neighbourhood centre.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In line with this, I am pleased to share with Members that Bukit Panjang constituency has started work to build a "Bukit Panjang Arts Street" at Bangkit neighbourhood centre.

sections.label: Tampines Town Hub and Yishun
sections.summary: A new Tampines Town Hub with sports facilities opens from end-2016, and Yishun has over 50,000 households with nearly 6,000 more moving in.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Chairman, a five-storey regional library, a 20-court badminton hall, six swimming pools and a 5,000-seat stadium with a Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA)-approved football pitch are some of the facilities residents can enjoy when the new Town Hub at Tampines opens progressively from the end of 2016.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Yishun is one of the largest and fastest growing towns in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We have over 50,000 households today and nearly 6,000 households moving in this year and next.

sections.label: Sports Facilities Master Plan funding
sections.summary: The $1.5 billion Sports Facilities Master Plan announced in 2014 is supposed to upgrade and rebuild community sports facilities.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the $1.5 billion Sports Facilities Master Plan announced in 2014, community sports facilities are supposed to be upgraded and rebuilt.

sections.label: National Youth Sports Institute launch
sections.summary: NYSI was announced in November 2015 and its first centre launched at Singapore Sports School in January 2016 to groom athletes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: The National Youth Sports Institute (NYSI) was announced in November 2015 and the first centre was officially launched at the Singapore Sports School (SSP) in January 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Aimed at grooming the "Champions of Tomorrow", NYSI is supposed to cover both athletes from SSP as well as mainstream schools' student-athletes.

sections.label: NYSI goals, KPIs and SSI
sections.summary: Questions are raised on NYSI's goals, KPIs, setup cost, qualified personnel, and how it complements the 2011 Singapore Sports Institute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: As NYSI is a new entity, it would also be interesting to know its goals and KPIs and the cost involved in setting it up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Do we have the required number of qualified sports scientists and sports personnel to oversee the running of these courses?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: There is also the Singapore Sports Institute (SSI), set up in 2011 to drive the high performance pathway in our local sports ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: How will NYSI complement SSI and are there overlaps?

sections.label: Support for Rio 2016 athletes
sections.summary: The passage asks what support will be provided to Team Singapore athletes competing in the Rio 2016 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What support will be provided to Team Singapore athletes who will be competing in this year's Rio 2016 Olympic and Paralympic Games?

sections.label: Disability sports engagement and support
sections.summary: The passage asks what MCCY and SportSG will do to engage persons with disability in sports and support para-athletes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Moving forward, I would like to ask what will MCCY and SportSG be doing to further engage persons with disability within our community to participate in sports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: What other measures are in place to create more social awareness about disability sports among the public?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And what more can SportSG do to provide the necessary support for our para-athletes?

sections.label: MCCY development status question
sections.summary: The speaker asks MCCY about the status of this development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: Can I ask MCCY on the status of this development?

sections.label: Individual Giving Survey 2014 findings
sections.summary: The 2014 NVPC Individual Giving Survey found one in five employers organised volunteer activities while one in two employees wanted employer-organised volunteering.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, according to the Individual Giving Survey in 2014 released by the NVPC last year, one in five employers organised volunteer activities but one in two employees expressed interest in employer-organised volunteering.

sections.label: Corporate giving roadmap and SME help
sections.summary: The speaker asks how MCCY's 2015 NVPC corporate giving roadmap increased donations and volunteering, and what plans exist to assist companies, especially SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In May 2015, MCCY announced that the NVPC would be developing a Singapore roadmap for corporate giving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: How has this plan helped to increase donations, both in cash and in kind, as well as volunteering from our corporations?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Some companies, particularly SMEs, need help or advice in how they can contribute.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: What plans does the Ministry have to engage and assist such companies?

sections.label: Business and IPC Partnership Scheme
sections.summary: The Budget's Business and IPC Partnership Scheme may spur corporate volunteerism, and the speaker notes foreign charitable trusts get exemptions that local citizens' trusts do not.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The introduction of the Business and Institution of a Public Character (IPC) Partnership Scheme in this Budget is likely to spur more corporations to encourage volunteerism amongst their employees and to contribute to the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: To this end, we have launched such initiatives as the Economic Development Board's (EDB's) International Organisations Programme Office (IOPO) for the setting up of International Non-Profit Organisations (INPOs) in Singapore, and the Commissioner of Charities' Foreign Charitable Purpose Trust (FCPT), under which charitable trusts set up by non-Singapore citizens or residents are exempted from registration and eligible for tax exemption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: All they want is giving and preferring their contributions to be discreet, they just want to leave behind a legacy or satisfy some personal and private sense of duty and gratitude.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, if they wished to set up a charitable trust in Singapore, they would be subject to greater administrative burdens and more onerous governance structures than FCPT, just because they are Singapore Citizens or residents.

sections.label: Harmonising foreign and local charity treatment
sections.summary: Harmonising treatment of foreign and local charities will encourage more charitable trusts in Singapore, whose assets likely benefit needy Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The harmonisation of treatment for charities set up by foreigners with those set up by locals will encourage more charitable trusts to be set up in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The assets of local trusts are likely to be held and managed in Singapore, and likely to benefit more needy Singaporeans.

sections.label: Religion freedom and secular state principles
sections.summary: The speaker says two principles maintain social cohesion: respecting freedom of religion and limiting it by respect for state secularity and the common good.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin, you have five minutes for your two cuts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There have been two principles that have helped us maintain a decent level of social cohesion thus far.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One, we have always been determined to respect freedom of religion; and, two, we have also been equally determined to let that freedom be limited by our respect for the secularity of the state, as well as our sense of responsibility towards the common good.

sections.label: Faith-and-reason modular programme suggestion
sections.summary: The speaker suggests developing a faith-and-reason modular programme for schools and external community platforms reaching young people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand the resistance to introducing anything resembling RK in the school curriculum ever again because implementation will always be complicated by the challenge of proselytisation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, can I suggest we develop a faith-and-reason modular programme to be run across schools as well as external community platforms reaching young people?

sections.label: Non-religious population and youths
sections.summary: The non-religious make up 18.5% of the population and more than half are youths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The non-religious make up 18.5% of our population and more than half are youths.

sections.label: Strategic roadmap for youth organisations
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MCCY develops a strategic roadmap guiding public, people and private youth organisations in building youth resilience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Outward Bound School (OBS) @ Coney is but one part of what must be a whole-of-sector strategy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope MCCY can develop a strategic roadmap that will guide the whole ecosystem of youth organisations from the public, people and private sectors to see their role in developing resilience in youths together.

sections.label: Platforms for youth interaction
sections.summary: The speaker says real-life platforms are needed for youth from different backgrounds to interact, and lauds the OBS @ Coney Island development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: It is, therefore, imperative that we create real-life platforms to bring youth from different backgrounds together so that they may interact, learn about one another and have open and frank conversations about their differences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: I, therefore, laud efforts like the development of the OBS @ Coney Island which has the great potential of being the platform to encourage healthy and organic interactions amongst our youths.

sections.label: New OBS on Coney Island
sections.summary: The speaker was heartened that the Government will soon build a new OBS on Coney Island, and believes every child should get an OBS opportunity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: I was thus heartened to hear that the Government will soon be building a new OBS on Coney Island to enhance the OBS experience for our youths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: I believe that every child should, at some point, be given the opportunity to spend time in OBS.

sections.label: OBS as youth rite-of-passage

sections.label: NVPC online giving platform
sections.summary: NVPC launched giving.sg to match citizens with causes and charities and let them track giving.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Last year, NVPC launched their online giving platform, giving.sg, to match citizens with causes and charities and enable them to track their giving activities.

sections.label: Silver Volunteer Fund
sections.summary: A Silver Volunteer Fund of up to $40 million was set up, championed by the President's Challenge and implemented by the Council for Third Age.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Last year, a Silver Volunteer Fund of up to $40 million was set up and it is championed by the President's Challenge.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: From this year, the fund will be implemented by the Council for Third Age, with support from NVPC.

sections.label: Company of Good Programme
sections.summary: NVPC partnered the Singapore Business Federation Foundation to develop a new Company of Good Programme for corporate giving capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Beyond these incentives, Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Henry Kwek asked how MCCY and NVPC are building up corporate giving capabilities in our businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that NVPC has partnered the Singapore Business Federation Foundation to develop a new Company of Good Programme.

sections.label: Basic training for businesses
sections.summary: NVPC will provide basic training to businesses starting giving programmes without prior experience.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: For businesses that are starting giving programmes without prior experience, NVPC will provide basic training.

sections.label: Team Nila volunteer expertise domains
sections.summary: SportSG will establish domains of expertise for Team Nila volunteers to use their skills through sports events.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To continue supporting the thousands of these Team Nila volunteers, SportSG will establish domains of expertise for volunteers to use their skills through sports events.

sections.label: Museum concessions for disabilities
sections.summary: MCCY will extend museum concessions to persons with disabilities, charging the lowest concession price and granting free access to one caregiver.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: MCCY will extend concessions to persons with disabilities at our NHB museums as well as the Singapore Art Museum and the National Gallery of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Those with disabilities will be charged the lowest concession price for permanent and special exhibitions, and we will grant free access to one accompanying caregiver.

sections.label: Centres of Expertise disability sports
sections.summary: SportSG will pilot Centres of Expertise with disability sports programmes and inclusive gyms, introducing them in at least five ActiveSG sports centres within five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: SportSG will pilot the launch of Centres of Expertise, which will have disability sports programmes and facilities like inclusive gyms that are more accessible to persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Within the next five years, we will introduce these in at least five ActiveSG sports centres island-wide, starting with centres in Queenstown, Sengkang, Toa Payoh and Jurong West.

sections.label: SportSG five-year initiatives with stakeholders
sections.summary: SportSG will develop and implement these initiatives with stakeholders over five years, creating common spaces and shared experiences through sports, heritage and arts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Together with stakeholders, SportSG will develop and implement these initiatives over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: At the same Page: 36 time, we also want to create common spaces and shared experiences through sports, heritage and arts, for us to come together, build stronger bonds and develop to our fullest potential.

sections.label: ActiveSG membership since 2014
sections.summary: ActiveSG, the national sports movement, has attracted more than one million members since its launch in April 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: As Minister Grace Fu shared, ActiveSG, our national movement for sports, has attracted more than one million members since its launch in April 2014.

sections.label: Public sports facility visitors
sections.summary: Last year, public sports facilities had more than 15 million visitors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Last year, our public sports facilities had more than 15 million visitors.

sections.label: Indoor sports halls and school fields
sections.summary: Under SFMP with MOE, 15 new indoor sports halls opened in 2015, with over 200,000 Dual-Use Scheme bookings, giving almost 80 indoor sports halls and close to 140 school fields.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: As part of SFMP, we have worked with MOE to open up 15 new indoor sports halls in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Over the last year, we have had more than 200,000 bookings for facilities under the Dual-Use Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: So, we now have almost 80 indoor sports halls and close to 140 school fields across the island available for public use after school hours.

sections.label: spexScholarship elite athlete support
sections.summary: More than 70 elite athletes from 16 different sports are under the spexScholarship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We are now providing our athletes with a wide range of support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We have more than 70 elite athletes from 16 different sports under the spexScholarship.

sections.label: spexBusiness Network and athletes
sections.summary: The spexBusiness Network tripled to 30 partners, with 72 athletes emplaced, and Singapore Sports School contributed 70 of 259 SEA Games medals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: The spexBusiness Network has tripled in size to 30 partners over the past two years and includes the likes of Deloitte and NTUC FairPrice, which were also sponsors of the SEA Games and ASEAN Para Games.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: To date, we have 72 athletes emplaced with these companies, so thank you for the support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Just last year, students and alumni from the Singapore Sports School contributed 70 out of 259 medals at the SEA Games.

sections.label: NYSI youth athlete support
sections.summary: In 2016 about 200 non-SSP youth athletes in nine sports will get NYSI support, rising to 400 carded youth national athletes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: For a start, in 2016, we expect about 200 non-SSP youth athletes, starting with nine identified sports, to benefit from the support by NYSI and its partners, including sport science and athlete life management services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: At steady state, NYSI will support up to 400 carded youth national athletes from mainstream schools.

sections.label: NAC-funded arts intermediaries
sections.summary: Intermediaries such as ArtsWok, Singapore Drama Educators Association, Art Outreach and National Book Development Council Singapore are funded by NAC's Major and Seed Grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Examples of such intermediaries include ArtsWok, the Singapore Drama Educators Association, Art Outreach and National Book Development Council Singapore and these Page: 40 are already being funded by NAC's Major and Seed Grants.

sections.label: NAC Major Grant framework review
sections.summary: NAC will review the Major Grant framework and welcomes ideas on improving the schemes, including KPIs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: In fact, NAC will be conducting a review of the Major Grant framework and we welcome ideas on how to improve the schemes, including KPIs.

sections.label: Armenian Street Party 2016 support
sections.summary: The Armenian Street Party 2016 was organised and supported by Bras Basah-Bugis Precinct stakeholders, including institutions, cultural groups and nearby shops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: For instance, the recent Armenian Street Party 2016 was organised and supported by stakeholders in the Bras Basah-Bugis Precinct, not just institutions like the Peranakan Museum and Singapore Management University, but also cultural groups like Dance Ensemble Singapore, the Peranakan community and shops in the vicinity.

sections.label: NAC traditional arts funding
sections.summary: NAC funding to traditional arts groups nearly doubled from $1.26 million in FY2011 to $2.51 million in FY2015, with over a third of Major Grant recipients being traditional arts groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: NAC's funding to traditional arts groups has almost doubled in the last five years from $1.26 million in FY2011 to $2.51 million in FY2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: In fact, in the recently announced list of NAC Major Grant recipients, more than one third are traditional arts groups.

sections.label: Taster programmes at five schools
sections.summary: These taster programmes will be introduced at five schools in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: As a start, we will introduce these taster programmes at five schools in 2016.

sections.label: WeCare Arts Fund and preschool arts
sections.summary: NAC and CDCs launched the WeCare Arts Fund in 2014, and NAC and ECDA signed a 2015 MOU on preschool arts education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: As part of ArtReach, NAC and the Community Development Councils (CDCs) launched the WeCare Arts Fund in 2014, comprising $1.5 million over three years, to support artist-led projects which promote arts to the less-privileged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: To date, we have supported a total of 115 VWOs; reaching out to 4,300 beneficiaries and conducting over 160 arts programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: NAC and ECDA also signed a two-year memorandum of understanding in April 2015 to implement new initiatives to promote and integrate arts education in preschools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: In 2016, the preschool Arts Education Programme will be expanded to 55 centres to bring even more arts programmes by professional artists and arts instructors to preschools.

sections.label: Pilot with NTUC My First Skool
sections.summary: NAC will pilot a whole-centre arts-based approach with NTUC My First Skool, starting at its new Edgefield Plains centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Expanding from these programmes, NAC will also pilot a whole-centre arts-based approach with anchor operator NTUC My First Skool (MFS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We will start with its new MFS Edgefield Plains centre in Punggol which is opening this June.

sections.label: Children's space at Goodman Arts Centre
sections.summary: NAC will dedicate a space within Goodman Arts Centre specifically for children's arts activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: While existing arts centres like The Esplanade and Aliwal Arts Centre will continue to feature family-friendly and children's programmes in their regular line-up of activities, NAC will dedicate a space within Goodman Arts Centre specifically for children's arts activities to give even more options to families and schools.

sections.label: Looking ahead to SG100
sections.summary: After SG50, the commitment is to partner citizens to realise a shared vision and build a better future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Following the SG50 Celebrations, as we take stock and look ahead to SG100, we are committed to partnering citizens to realise our shared vision and to build a better future for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: Duration of Our Singapore Fund
sections.summary: The question asks whether there is a duration to the $25 million set aside for ground-up initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: First, on Our Singapore Fund, the $25 million that was set aside for ground-up initiatives, is there a duration to the sum?

sections.label: Museum and National Gallery visits
sections.summary: The Minister stated there are four million museum visits and 700,000 National Gallery visits.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Minister mentioned that there are four million visits to our museums and 700,000 visits now to the National Gallery.

sections.label: Museum visitor breakdown and free admission
sections.summary: The Minister could not give a foreigner-local breakdown but recalled about one-third foreigners and two-thirds locals, and noted free museum admission was well-received.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: For museum numbers, I am not able to give the Member the numbers in terms of breakdown of foreigners and locals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: But if my memory serves me right, for the National Gallery and museum, we have a sizeable number that is made up of foreigners, probably about one-third foreigners, two-thirds locals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: As Members would remember, we extended free admission to our museums and that has been quite well-received.

sections.label: Building OBS @ Coney
sections.summary: The priority is to build OBS @ Coney to reach out extensively to Secondary 3 cohorts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Having said that, our priority right now is to build OBS @ Coney so that it can have the capacity to allow us to reach out extensively to the Secondary 3 cohorts of our students.

sections.label: Asatizah Recognition Scheme registration questions
sections.summary: The speaker said the system will adapt to MOE's new system, noted 80% of asatizahs are registered under ARS, and asked two clarifications.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: We will take guidance from MOE but, certainly, we will make sure that our system is ready to accommodate and adapt to the new system that MOE will put in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I am heartened that 80% of our asatizahs are registered under the Asatizah Recognition Scheme (ARS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: My two clarifications are: first, will all teachers teaching Islamic education be required to register under this scheme?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Second, what is the basic qualification required to be registered and assessed to be having the knowledge and competency to teach Islamic education?

sections.label: Making ARS mandatory
sections.summary: The speaker said the question is almost whether to make ARS mandatory and wants to encourage the 20% to come onboard.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: To the first question, it is almost whether we should make the ARS mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: And as I mentioned in my reply, we want to encourage the 20% to come onboard.

sections.label: Discourse, dissent and advisories
sections.summary: The speaker said discourse, dissent and disagreements can take place in Singapore through classification and advisories.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Having these considerations in mind, I think discourse, dissent, disagreements can take place and have their place in Singapore, and we do that by classification, by giving advisories.

sections.label: Diversity in Singapore arts
sections.summary: The passage states that uncomfortable topics and dissenting issues now get a hearing and place in the arts, with more variety and diversity allowed over time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In terms of diversity, too, topics that were perhaps uncomfortable in the past, whether they deal with specific lifestyles or values, or deal with issues, such as conservation of an environment – I think Mr Kok recently also did a work on Bukit Brown – issues that arouse disagreement and dissent in the society get a hearing, get their place in the arts, including works like "Gemuk Girls" which has criticised parts of the political system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We have, over time, allowed more variety, greater diversity in artworks.

sections.label: Traditional Arts Master Plan support
sections.summary: The passage states NAC is providing more support to traditional arts groups through the Traditional Arts Master Plan, covering production, training and audience development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Since traditional arts have a long history, the technical skills required can take a long time to train, for example, in the case of dance and Chinese opera.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Hence, NAC is providing more support to traditional arts groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: The Traditional Arts Master Plan will provide more resources to these arts groups, not only in production and training, but also helping them develop their audiences.

sections.label: Outreach since 9/11
sections.summary: The passage states that since 9/11, work has been done to reach out, especially for the Malay/Muslim community.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Since 9/11, we have been working very hard, especially for the Malay/Muslim community, to reach out.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim institutions integration assurance
sections.summary: The passage states that MUIS, mosques and madrasahs will continue to find ways to integrate with the wider community.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: On the part of the Malay/Muslim community, I would like to assure the House that our various institutions, MUIS, mosques, madrasahs, will continue to do our best to find ways and means to integrate with the wider community.

sections.label: Yishun sporting facilities delay
sections.summary: The passage states that Yishun residents will have to wait beyond 2020 for sporting facilities because of constraints on contractors' capacity.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If I heard and understood the Parliamentary Secretary correctly, residents in Yishun will have to wait beyond 2020 for the sporting facilities because of the constraint on the contractors' capacity.

sections.label: Yishun swimming pool repairs
sections.summary: The passage states that SportSG has been instructed to look at the Yishun swimming pool and whether repairs are needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: You are very concerned about the swimming pool.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We have instructed SportSG to specially look at the swimming pool in Yishun, whether there are any repairs that are needed to be done.

sections.label: Madrasah collaboration with MUIS
sections.summary: Madrasah Aljunied and Arabiah, under JMS, are rolling out new programmes with MUIS, which the speaker commends as making madrasahs more progressive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since the Minister had mentioned just now that Madrasah Aljunied and Arabiah, which are under JMS, in collaboration with MUIS, are rolling out new programmes, I commend these collaborative efforts in making madrasahs a more progressive institution.

sections.label: Coney Island funding and EIA
sections.summary: Half of the $250 million covers first-mover infrastructure on Coney Island, facilities cost about half, and an EIA will be conducted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Of that $250 million that we have spoken about, half of it has to do with being the first-mover onto Coney Island and having the need to lay down infrastructure, power, electricity, boats and so on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: That is the reason why the overall figure for the funds needed seemed high.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The amount needed to build the facilities per se is about half of the amount.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: On the second point about whether we will be conducting an EIA, the answer is yes.

sections.label: OBS Coney Island ferry logistics
sections.summary: OBS @ Coney is important because tripling capacity on a ferry-only island would strain logistics tremendously.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Yes, the reason why OBS @ Coney is such an important location for us is because for us to ramp up the capacity by three times on an island that is only connected by ferry would have cost a tremendous strain on logistics.

sections.label: Dissent works and Gemuk Girls
sections.summary: Works showing dissent exist, including the play "Gemuk Girls" put up by a funded group.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: As I explained earlier on, there have been works that showed dissent, including what I have just mentioned, this play about "Gemuk Girls" that has been put up by one of the groups that has received funding.

sections.label: Funding for critical arts groups
sections.summary: The speaker disagrees that funding was withheld from arts groups critical of the Government, saying many remain funded and some had increases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, there will be tension always but, as an art promoter, we will work as much as we can to facilitate respectful discussions among the artists, the arts industry, as well as the regulator.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, I do not agree with what the Member has said that we have withheld funding from arts groups that have been critical of the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Many of the arts groups that have put up plays, that have been critical of the Government, continue to be funded.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In fact, some have had their funding increased over the years.

sections.label: OBS campus and capacity costs
sections.summary: $45 million links the OBS campus to water and sewage, and $75 million covers staff, equipment and programming to triple capacity safely.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Forty-five million dollars is needed to link the OBS campus to basic facilities, such as water and sewage, and $75 million has to do with increased staff, equipment and programming costs, to ensure safety as we triple the capacity of OBS.
